claim: Zebrafish cartilages undergo extensive remodeling and vascularization during juvenile stages to generate fat-filled bones.
source: We find that zebrafish cartilages undergo extensive remodeling and vascularization during juvenile stages to generate fat-filled bones.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1 and vascularization data in Figure 2, as well as direct observation of the developmental process.

claim: Growth plate chondrocytes marked by sox10 and col2a1a contribute to osteoblasts, marrow adipocytes, and mesenchymal cells within adult bones.
source: Growth plate chondrocytes marked by sox10 and col2a1a contribute to osteoblasts, marrow adipocytes, and mesenchymal cells within adult bones.
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing experiments using sox10:CreERT2 and col2a1a:CreERT2 lines shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: At the edge of the hypertrophic zone, chondrocytes re-enter the cell cycle and express leptin receptor (lepr), suggesting conversion into progenitors.
source: At the edge of the hypertrophic zone, chondrocytes re-enter the cell cycle and express leptin receptor (lepr), suggesting conversion into progenitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data in Figure 6B and RNAscope in situ hybridization for lepr in Figure 6C-D.

claim: Mutation of matrix metalloproteinase 9 (mmp9) results in delayed growth plate remodeling and fewer marrow adipocytes.
source: Further, mutation of matrix metalloproteinase 9 (mmp9) results in delayed growth plate remodeling and fewer marrow adipocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of mmp9 mutants shown in Figure 7, including quantification of growth plate width and adipocyte numbers.

claim: Mmp9-dependent growth plate remodeling and conversion of chondrocytes into osteoblasts and marrow adipocytes are conserved features of bony vertebrates.
source: Our data support Mmp9-dependent growth plate remodeling and conversion of chondrocytes into osteoblasts and marrow adipocytes as conserved features of bony vertebrates.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of zebrafish data with known mammalian biology, supported by experimental data in Figures 1-7.

claim: Zebrafish have intramembranous and endochondral bones.
source: As with mammals, zebrafish also have intramembranous and endochondral bones.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established knowledge in the field.

claim: Zebrafish endochondral bones are hollow and filled predominantly with fat yet do not support hematopoiesis as in mammals.
source: Their endochondral bones are hollow and filled predominantly with fat yet do not support hematopoiesis as in mammals (Witten and Huysseune, 2009; Weigele and Franz-Odendaal, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Many hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo cell death during endochondral ossification, with osteoblasts forming from periosteal cells brought into the bone along with the vasculature.
source: It has long been appreciated that many hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo cell death during endochondral ossification, with osteoblasts forming from periosteal cells brought into the bone along with the vasculature (Maes et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established knowledge in the field.

claim: Cultured chondrocytes can dedifferentiate into mesenchymal progenitors and/or transdifferentiate into osteoblasts.
source: At the same time, there are numerous studies showing that cultured chondrocytes can dedifferentiate into mesenchymal progenitors and/or transdifferentiate into osteoblasts (Shimomura et al., 1975; Mayne et al., 1976; von der Mark and von der Mark, 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous in vitro studies.

claim: Lineage tracing studies in mouse using Col10a1-Cre- and Aggrecan-Cre-based transgenes revealed that hypertrophic chondrocytes make a major contribution to osteoblasts within trabecular bone and potentially also the bone collar.
source: Recent lineage tracing studies of hypertrophic chondrocytes, using constitutive and inducible Col10a1-Cre- and Aggrecan-Cre-based transgenes in mice, has revealed that such transdifferentiation may also occur in vivo, with chondrocytes making a major contribution to osteoblasts within trabecular bone and potentially also the bone collar (Yang et al., 2014; Kobayashi et al., 2014; Jing et al., 2015; Park et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous mouse lineage tracing studies.

claim: The ceratohyal (Ch) bone is derived from cranial neural crest cells.
source: This long bone, which is derived from cranial neural crest cells, exhibits properties in common with the long bones of mammalian limbs, including two prominent growth plates at either end and a marrow cavity (Paul et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The Ch bone exhibits properties in common with the long bones of mammalian limbs, including two prominent growth plates at either end and a marrow cavity.
source: This long bone, which is derived from cranial neural crest cells, exhibits properties in common with the long bones of mammalian limbs, including two prominent growth plates at either end and a marrow cavity (Paul et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study and anatomical observations.

claim: At 11 mm standard length (approx. 4.5 weeks post-fertilization), the Ch contains chondrocytes throughout its length with the exception of a small marrow space at the anterior tip.
source: At 11 mm standard length (SL) (approx. 4.5 weeks post-fertilization (wpf)), the Ch contains chondrocytes throughout its length with the exception of a small marrow space at the anterior tip.
evidence: This claim is supported by pentachrome staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Ch is surrounded by a thin layer of cortical bone that has been shown to derive from osteoblasts located on the outside of the cartilage template (i.e. periosteum).
source: The Ch is surrounded by a thin layer of cortical bone that has been shown to derive from osteoblasts located on the outside of the cartilage template (i.e. periosteum) (Paul et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: By 12 mm SL (approx. five wpf), both tips of the Ch contain marrow spaces, and on the central sides of the growth plates we begin to observe small fissures in the cortical bone and disruption of the hypertrophic zone.
source: By 12 mm SL (approx. five wpf), both tips of the Ch contain marrow spaces, and on the central sides of the growth plates we begin to observe small fissures in the cortical bone and disruption of the hypertrophic zone.
evidence: This claim is supported by pentachrome staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: By 13 mm SL (approx. 5.5 wpf), breaks in the cortical bone become more prominent and are accompanied by further degradation of the cartilage matrix.
source: By 13 mm SL (approx. 5.5 wpf), breaks in the cortical bone become more prominent and are accompanied by further degradation of the cartilage matrix.
evidence: This claim is supported by pentachrome staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At later stages (16 and 19 mm SL) (approx. 7 and 9 wpf), cortical bone regains integrity and increases in thickness, and marrow adipocytes containing LipidTOX+ lipid vesicles are seen throughout Ch.
source: At later stages (16 and 19 mm SL) (approx. 7 and 9 wpf), cortical bone regains integrity and increases in thickness, and marrow adipocytes containing LipidTOX +lipid vesicles are seen throughout Ch (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by pentachrome staining data in Figure 1B and LipidTOX staining in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: By adulthood (one year of age), the marrow cavity is filled with large fat cells and the growth plates appear largely mineralized.
source: By adulthood (one year of age), the marrow cavity is filled with large fat cells and the growth plates appear largely mineralized.
evidence: This claim is supported by pentachrome staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A number of other cartilage-derived bones in the face and fins have been reported to have a similar structure in zebrafish, including growth plates and prominent marrow fat.
source: While we focus on the Ch for this study, a number of other cartilage-derived bones in the face and fins have been reported to have a similar structure in zebrafish, including growth plates and prominent marrow fat (Weigele and Franz-Odendaal, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: At 10 and 11 mm SL, vessels expressing fli1a:GFP are found largely on the outside of the Ch bone.
source: At 10 and 11 mm SL, vessels expressing fli1a:GFP are found largely on the outside of the Ch bone.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: By 13, 16, and 20 mm SL, we observe increasing numbers of capillaries within the Ch, coinciding with the replacement of col2a1a:mCherry-NTR+ chondrocytes with adipocytes.
source: By 13, 16, and 20 mm SL, we observe increasing numbers of capillaries within the Ch, coinciding with the replacement of col2a1a:mCherry-NTR +chondrocytes with adipocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At 28 mm SL (approx. 26 wpf), the Ch is heavily supplied with both kdrl:GFP+ blood vessels and lyve1:DsRed+ lymphatic vessels, which abut each side of the growth plate.
source: At 28 mm SL (approx. 26 wpf), the Ch is heavily supplied with both kdrl:GFP+blood vessels and lyve1:DsRed+lymphatic vessels, which abut each side of the growth plate (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Remodeling of the Ch bone is accompanied by extensive vascular invasion of the cartilage template.
source: Hence, as in mammalian bones, remodeling of the Ch bone is accompanied by extensive vascular invasion of the cartilage template.
evidence: This claim is supported by vascularization data shown in Figure 2 and comparison to mammalian biology.

claim: The zebrafish sox10 promoter drives expression in early cranial neural crest cells from 10 to 16 hpf, followed by a second wave of expression in all chondrocytes from two dpf onwards.
source: The zebrafish sox10 promoter drives expression in early cranial neural crest cells from 10 to 16 hpf, followed by a second wave of expression in all chondrocytes from two dpf onwards (Dutton et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Upon addition of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) at 15 dpf, we observed extensive labeling of chondrocytes within 5 days, as well as some cells in the perichondrium surrounding Ch and other cartilages.
source: Upon addition of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) at 15 dpf, we observed extensive labeling of chondrocytes within 5 days, as well as some cells in the perichondrium surrounding Ch and other cartilages (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: We did not observe leaky conversion in the absence of 4-OHT at either embryonic or adult stages.
source: We did not observe leaky conversion in the absence of 4-OHT at either embryonic or adult stages (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In sections through the middle of Ch, we observed labeling of a number of large diameter cells of adipocyte morphology.
source: In sections through the middle of Ch, we observed labeling of a number of large diameter cells of adipocyte morphology (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In superficial sections through the cortical bone, we also observed labeled cells that were positive for the osteoblast marker ocn:GFP, as well as some labeled cells negative for ocn:GFP that may represent bone progenitors or other cell types.
source: In superficial sections through the cortical bone, we also observed labeled cells that were positive for the osteoblast marker ocn:GFP, as well as some labeled cells negative for ocn:GFP that may represent bone progenitors or other cell types (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The Ch bone is neural crest-derived.
source: This is consistent with previous studies showing that the Ch bone is neural crest-derived (Schilling and Kimmel, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study and lineage tracing data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: We also detect unconverted cells in the marrow, consistent with contribution of non-neural crest-derived cells such as the mesoderm-derived vasculature.
source: However, we also detect unconverted cells in the marrow, consistent with contribution of non-neural crest-derived cells such as the mesoderm-derived vasculature (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and vascularization data in Figure 2.

claim: When analyzed at 30 mm SL, growth plate clones could be quite large, consistent with clonal selection as described in the zebrafish heart and skeletal muscle.
source: When analyzed at 30 mm SL, growth plate clones could be quite large, consistent with clonal selection as described in the zebrafish heart and skeletal muscle (Gupta and Poss, 2012; Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by clonal analysis data in Figure 3E and citations to previous studies.

claim: We observed a clone that contributed to a narrow column of growth plate chondrocytes in the middle of Ch that was contiguous with mesenchymal cells and then adipocytes toward the central marrow cavity.
source: In one example with three discrete clones, we observed a clone that contributed to a narrow column of growth plate chondrocytes in the middle of Ch that was contiguous with mesenchymal cells and then adipocytes toward the central marrow cavity (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by clonal analysis data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Analysis of uniquely colored clones in the growth plate revealed those that contained both chondrocytes and adjacent adipocytes in the marrow.
source: Analysis of uniquely colored clones in the growth plate revealed those that contained both chondrocytes and adjacent adipocytes in the marrow (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Zebrabow clonal analysis data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: We also observed clones that appeared to contain chondrocytes and weakly labeled cells embedded in cortical bone, though the clonal contribution to these and other mesenchymal lineages will require further analysis.
source: We also observed clones that appeared to contain chondrocytes and weakly labeled cells embedded in cortical bone, though the clonal contribution to these and other mesenchymal lineages will require further analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by clonal analysis data in Figure 3F but acknowledges uncertainty.

claim: Our data are consistent with chondrocytes giving rise to adipocytes and mesenchymal cells, and potentially osteoblasts, after growth plate remodeling in zebrafish.
source: Together, our data are consistent with chondrocytes giving rise to adipocytes and mesenchymal cells, and potentially osteoblasts, after growth plate remodeling in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: In mice, Col2a1:CreERT2-mediated conversion at embryonic and early postnatal stages broadly labels not only chondrocytes but also osteochondroprogenitors, such as those in the perichondrium and periosteum.
source: In mice, Col2a1:CreERT2-mediated conversion at embryonic and early postnatal stages broadly labels not only chondrocytes but also osteochondroprogenitors, such as those in the perichondrium and periosteum (Ono et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous mouse study.

claim: In zebrafish, col2a1a is similarly expressed at high levels in chondrocytes and in weaker levels in osteoblasts and perichondrium, although direct evidence for col2a1a marking osteochondroprogenitors in zebrafish is lacking.
source: In zebrafish, col2a1a is similarly expressed at high levels in chondrocytes and in weaker levels in osteoblasts and perichondrium, although direct evidence for col2a1a marking osteochondroprogenitors in zebrafish is lacking (Eames et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Treatment of col2a1a/B > R fish with a single dose of 4-OHT at five dpf resulted in extensive labeling of col2a1a-BAC:GFP+ chondrocytes at 12 dpf, but no labeling of the perichondrium, periosteum, and osteoblasts as marked by the sp7:GFP transgene.
source: Treatment of col2a1a/B > R fish with a single dose of 4-OHT at five dpf resulted in extensive labeling of col2a1a-BAC:GFP+ chondrocytes at 12 dpf, but no labeling of the perichondrium, periosteum, and osteoblasts as marked by the sp7:GFP transgene (Figure 4A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 4A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: We also observed labeling of the notochord in larval fish, but no labeling of the vasculature, blood, or other tissues examined.
source: We also observed labeling of the notochord in larval fish, but no labeling of the vasculature, blood, or other tissues examined.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from lineage tracing experiments.

claim: After conversion of col2a1a/B > R chondrocytes at five dpf and examination at adulthood (30 mm SL), maximal intensity projections through Ch revealed extensive labeling of growth plate chondrocytes, as well as cells throughout the bone and marrow cavity.
source: After conversion of col2a1a/B > R chondrocytes at five dpf and examination at adulthood (30 mm SL), maximal intensity projections through Ch revealed extensive labeling of growth plate chondrocytes, as well as cells throughout the bone and marrow cavity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The majority of adult growth plate chondrocytes in Ch appear to derive from embryonic chondrocytes.
source: Thus, the majority of adult growth plate chondrocytes in Ch appear to derive from embryonic chondrocytes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the extensive labeling of adult growth plate chondrocytes after embryonic conversion shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Optical sections revealed cytoplasmic DsRed staining in lipid-filled adipocytes, presumptive osteoblasts lining the inner surface of bone, and mesenchymal cells within the marrow cavity.
source: Moreover, optical sections revealed cytoplasmic DsRed staining in lipid-filled adipocytes, presumptive osteoblasts lining the inner surface of bone, and mesenchymal cells within the marrow cavity.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In some animals displaying lower conversion efficiency, we observed apparent clones of cells containing growth plate chondrocytes, large adipocytes, and osteoblasts embedded in Calcein+ mineralized matrix.
source: In some animals displaying lower conversion efficiency, we observed apparent clones of cells containing growth plate chondrocytes, large adipocytes, and osteoblasts embedded in Calcein +mineralized matrix (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by clonal analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Analysis of individual sections at higher magnification revealed contribution of col2a1a-lineage cells to a subset of osteoblasts within both the endosteal and periosteal surfaces of bone, as well as embedded osteocytes with characteristic cellular processes.
source: Analysis of individual sections at higher magnification revealed contribution of col2a1a-lineage cells to a subset of osteoblasts within both the endosteal and periosteal surfaces of bone, as well as embedded osteocytes with characteristic cellular processes (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by high-magnification confocal imaging data shown in Figure 4E-G.

claim: An advantage of the Histone2A-mCherry lineage approach is that the levels of Histone2A-mCherry protein, which is stably incorporated into chromatin, reflect those of endogenous col2a1a in chondrocytes provided continued cell division does not dilute out the fusion protein.
source: An advantage of this type of lineage approach is that the levels of Histone2A-mCherry protein, which is stably incorporated into chromatin, reflect those of endogenous col2a1a in chondrocytes provided continued cell division does not dilute out the fusion protein.
evidence: This claim is based on the known properties of histone fusion proteins and their behavior during cell division.

claim: In zebrafish, col2a1a is expressed at high levels in the proliferative zone of the Ch growth plate and then downregulated in the hypertrophic zone.
source: In zebrafish, col2a1a is expressed at high levels in the proliferative zone of the Ch growth plate and then downregulated in the hypertrophic zone (Paul et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In a newly generated col2a1a:Histone2A-mCherry-T2A-GFP-CAAX transgenic line, membrane-localized GFP-CAAX, which is rapidly turned over, is seen primarily in the proliferative zone, whereas Histone2A-mCherry is seen uniformly throughout the Ch cartilage, confirming the long-lived nature of this fusion protein.
source: In a newly generated col2a1a:Histone2A-mCherry-T2A-GFP-CAAX transgenic line, membrane-localized GFP-CAAX, which is rapidly turned over, is seen primarily in the proliferative zone, whereas Histone2A-mCherry is seen uniformly throughout the Ch cartilage, confirming the long-lived nature of this fusion protein (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: At 7–8 mm SL (approx. three wpf), which is well before the start of growth plate remodeling at 11–12 mm SL, all Ch chondrocytes are Histone2A-mCherry+ and we do not detect Histone2A-mCherry+ cells associated with Calcein Blue+ bone or co-expressing the osteoblast transgene ocn:GFP.
source: At 7–8 mm SL (approx. three wpf), which is well before the start of growth plate remodeling at 11–12 mm SL, all Ch chondrocytes are Histone2A-mCherry+ and we do not detect Histone2A-mCherry+ cells associated with Calcein Blue+ bone or co-expressing the osteoblast transgene ocn:GFP (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: At post-remodeling stages (12 and 18 mm SL), we observe extensive overlap of Histone2A-mCherry with ocn:GFP+ osteoblasts associated with cortical bone.
source: In contrast, at post-remodeling stages (12 and 18 mm SL), we observe extensive overlap of Histone2A-mCherry with ocn:GFP+ osteoblasts associated with cortical bone (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: We also observe numerous Histone2A-mCherry+ cells embedded in the endosteal and periosteal surfaces of the Ch bone (labeled by Calcein Blue), with several of these cells co-expressing the pre-osteoblast transgene RUNX2:GFP or the early osteoblast transgene sp7:GFP.
source: We also observe numerous Histone2A-mCherry+ cells embedded in the endosteal and periosteal surfaces of the Ch bone (labeled by Calcein Blue), with several of these cells co-expressing the pre-osteoblast transgene RUNX2:GFP or the early osteoblast transgene sp7:GFP (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: We observed that sp7:GFP+ osteoblasts further from the growth plate tended to have weaker Histone2A-mCherry signal than those more closely associated with the edge of the hypertrophic zone, suggesting that hypertrophic chondrocytes and/or their osteoblast derivatives undergo cell division to dilute out the Histone2A-mCherry signal.
source: In addition, we observed that sp7:GFP+ osteoblasts further from the growth plate tended to have weaker Histone2A-mCherry signal than those more closely associated with the edge of the hypertrophic zone, suggesting that hypertrophic chondrocytes and/or their osteoblast derivatives undergo cell division to dilute out the Histone2A-mCherry signal.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from confocal imaging data and inference about cell division.

claim: These findings independently confirm the conclusions of our CreER lineage tracing studies that col2a1a+ chondrocytes generate osteoblasts in zebrafish.
source: These findings independently confirm the conclusions of our CreER lineage tracing studies that col2a1a+ chondrocytes generate osteoblasts in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Histone2A-mCherry lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5.

claim: At the beginning of remodeling (11 mm SL), we detected BrdU+ cells in the central zone of chondroblasts in the growth plate, as well as in the perichondrium and periosteum.
source: At the beginning of remodeling (11 mm SL), we detected BrdU+ cells in the central zone of chondroblasts in the growth plate, as well as in the perichondrium and periosteum.
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: We observed BrdU+ cells at the edge of the hypertrophic zone where the cartilage matrix is being actively degraded, similar to what has been reported in mouse.
source: In addition, we observed BrdU+ cells at the edge of the hypertrophic zone where the cartilage matrix is being actively degraded, similar to what has been reported in mouse (Park et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6B and citation to a mouse study.

claim: We observed BrdU incorporation in similarly positioned hypertrophic chondrocytes at 15 and 19 mm SL, with BrdU+ cells becoming fewer in the perichondrium and periosteum by 19 mm.
source: We observed BrdU incorporation in similarly positioned hypertrophic chondrocytes at 15 and 19 mm SL, with BrdU+ cells becoming fewer in the perichondrium and periosteum by 19 mm.
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In mice, LepR expression marks a heterogeneous population of cells in endochondral bone, including a putative postnatal skeletal stem cell population.
source: In mice, LepR expression marks a heterogeneous population of cells in endochondral bone, including a putative postnatal skeletal stem cell population (Zhou et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous mouse study.

claim: A comparison with the hypertrophic chondrocyte and early osteoblast marker runx2b shows higher lepr expression in proliferative versus hypertrophic chondrocytes at 8, 12, and 20 mm SL stages, with chondrocyte expression decreasing by 27 mm SL.
source: A comparison with the hypertrophic chondrocyte and early osteoblast marker runx2b shows higher lepr expression in proliferative versus hypertrophic chondrocytes at 8, 12, and 20 mm SL stages, with chondrocyte expression decreasing by 27 mm SL (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: During remodeling of zebrafish Ch (15 mm SL), we also observe lepr+ cells in the marrow cavity that are derived from chondrocytes, based on labeling by col2a1a/B > R.
source: During remodeling of zebrafish Ch (15 mm SL), we also observe lepr+ cells in the marrow cavity that are derived from chondrocytes, based on labeling by col2a1a/B > R (Figure 6C), and we continue to observe lepr+ cells in the Ch marrow at later stages (20 and 27 mm SL) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization combined with lineage tracing shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: These results are consistent with lepr+ cells in the bone marrow deriving from growth plate chondrocytes in zebrafish, although direct evidence will be needed to determine if any of these chondrocyte-derived lepr+ marrow cells behave as skeletal stem cells in zebrafish.
source: These results are consistent with lepr+ cells in the bone marrow deriving from growth plate chondrocytes in zebrafish, although direct evidence will be needed to determine if any of these chondrocyte-derived lepr+ marrow cells behave as skeletal stem cells in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is based on the lepr expression and lineage tracing data, but acknowledges that functional evidence is still needed.

claim: In mice, Mmp9 has been reported to function in hematopoietic lineage cells for growth plate remodeling, as bone marrow transplants can rescue the delay in growth plate remodeling seen in Mmp9 mutants.
source: In mice, Mmp9 has been reported to function in hematopoietic lineage cells for growth plate remodeling, as bone marrow transplants can rescue the delay in growth plate remodeling seen in Mmp9 mutants (Vu et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous mouse study.

claim: At the beginning of remodeling (11 mm SL), we observe expression of mmp9 at the edge of the hypertrophic zone, with this restricted expression in late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes continuing through 17 mm SL stages.
source: At the beginning of remodeling (11 mm SL), we observe expression of mmp9 at the edge of the hypertrophic zone, with this restricted expression in late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes continuing through 17 mm SL stages (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Higher magnification views show that mmp9 expression is prominent in hypertrophic chondrocytes that appear to be exiting their lacunae.
source: Higher magnification views show that mmp9 expression is prominent in hypertrophic chondrocytes that appear to be exiting their lacunae.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: mmp9 homozygous mutants are adult viable and do not display obvious larval craniofacial defects.
source: mmp9 homozygous mutants are adult viable and do not display obvious larval craniofacial defects.
evidence: This claim is based on observations of mmp9 mutant zebrafish.

claim: Whereas trichrome staining revealed no significant differences in the mutant Ch growth plates at 17 mm SL, by 21 mm we observed that the hypertrophic zone was significantly larger, compared to the proliferative zone, in mmp9 mutants versus controls, indicating a delay in growth plate remodeling.
source: Whereas trichrome staining revealed no significant differences in the mutant Ch growth plates at 17 mm SL, by 21 mm we observed that the hypertrophic zone was significantly larger, compared to the proliferative zone, in mmp9 mutants versus controls, indicating a delay in growth plate remodeling (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by trichrome staining and quantification shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: The defect in growth plate remodeling was still evident at 27 mm SL, with mutants displaying a wider Ch growth plate.
source: The defect in growth plate remodeling was still evident at 27 mm SL, with mutants displaying a wider Ch growth plate (Figure 7E,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging and quantification shown in Figure 7E,G.

claim: mmp9 mutants also had fewer adipocytes in the central marrow cavity compared to stage-matched controls, consistent with adipocytes deriving from hypertrophic chondrocytes that are released from the cartilage matrix by Mmp9 activity.
source: Strikingly, mmp9 mutants also had fewer adipocytes in the central marrow cavity compared to stage-matched controls (Figure 7E,G), consistent with adipocytes deriving from hypertrophic chondrocytes that are released from the cartilage matrix by Mmp9 activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging and quantification shown in Figure 7E,G and inference about the mechanism.

claim: At adult stages, we were able to recover eight mutant recipients with contribution of wild-type cells to chondrocytes of the Ch growth plate.
source: At adult stages, we were able to recover eight mutant recipients with contribution of wild-type cells to chondrocytes of the Ch growth plate.
evidence: This claim is based on neural crest transplantation experiments.

claim: In these animals, we observed a rescue of growth plate width, with a trend toward better rescue in wild-type versus mutant regions of the growth plate (p = 0.06), as well as a trend toward rescue of adipocyte number (p = 0.06).
source: In these animals, we observed a rescue of growth plate width, with a trend toward better rescue in wild-type versus mutant regions of the growth plate (p = 0.06), as well as a trend toward rescue of adipocyte number (p = 0.06) (Figure 7E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by neural crest transplantation experiments and quantification shown in Figure 7E-G.

claim: As a control, transplantation of wild-type neural crest cells into wild-type animals had no effect on Ch growth plate width and adipocyte number.
source: As a control, transplantation of wild-type neural crest cells into wild-type animals had no effect on Ch growth plate width and adipocyte number.
evidence: This claim is based on control transplantation experiments.

claim: These results indicate that mmp9 is required in the neural crest lineage, and potentially chondrocytes themselves, for efficient remodeling of the growth plate and the generation of marrow adipocytes from chondrocytes.
source: These results indicate that mmp9 is required in the neural crest lineage, and potentially chondrocytes themselves, for efficient remodeling of the growth plate and the generation of marrow adipocytes from chondrocytes.
evidence: This claim is based on the neural crest transplantation rescue experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Despite anatomical differences between zebrafish and mammalian bones, we find that growth plate remodeling is remarkably well conserved and thus likely ancestral to bony vertebrates.
source: Despite anatomical differences between zebrafish and mammalian bones, we find that growth plate remodeling is remarkably well conserved and thus likely ancestral to bony vertebrates.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of zebrafish data with mammalian biology and evolutionary inference.

claim: The zebrafish Ch undergoes a transient breakdown of cortical bone near the growth plates, which coincides with extensive vascularization and an Mmp9-dependent replacement of hypertrophic chondrocytes with fat and bone.
source: The zebrafish Ch undergoes a transient breakdown of cortical bone near the growth plates, which coincides with extensive vascularization and an Mmp9-dependent replacement of hypertrophic chondrocytes with fat and bone.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1, 2, and 7.

claim: Using multiple methods of lineage tracing, including a Cre-independent technique, we show that late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes generate not only osteoblasts but also marrow adipocytes in zebrafish.
source: Using multiple methods of lineage tracing, including a Cre-independent technique, we show that late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes generate not only osteoblasts but also marrow adipocytes in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figures 3, 4, and 5.

claim: Further support for the ability of chondrocytes to generate adipocytes is that delayed growth plate remodeling in mmp9 mutants results in a paucity of marrow adipocytes in adults.
source: Further support for the ability of chondrocytes to generate adipocytes is that delayed growth plate remodeling in mmp9 mutants results in a paucity of marrow adipocytes in adults.
evidence: This claim is supported by mmp9 mutant analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: We show that hypertrophic chondrocytes re-enter the cell cycle and contribute to lepr+ mesenchymal cells, raising the possibility that partial dedifferentiation into proliferative progenitors underlies chondrocyte fate transitions inside endochondral bones.
source: Lastly, we show that hypertrophic chondrocytes re-enter the cell cycle and contribute to lepr+ mesenchymal cells, raising the possibility that partial dedifferentiation into proliferative progenitors underlies chondrocyte fate transitions inside endochondral bones.
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU incorporation and lepr expression data shown in Figure 6.

claim: We find significant contribution of chondrocyte-derived cells to both the endosteal and periosteal surfaces of the Ch bone, similar to what has been described in the mouse.
source: However, we find significant contribution of chondrocyte-derived cells to both the endosteal and periosteal surfaces of the Ch bone, similar to what has been described in the mouse (Yang et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2014a; Jing et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data in Figures 3-5 and citations to mouse studies.

claim: We also reveal chondrocytes to be a significant source of marrow adipocytes in zebrafish.
source: We also reveal chondrocytes to be a significant source of marrow adipocytes in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: There are likely other sources for osteoblasts and marrow adipocytes, in particular the periosteum which houses several types of skeletal stem cells.
source: Our findings raise the question of whether marrow adipocytes also derive in part from chondrocytes in mammals. Indeed, older studies have demonstrated the ability of murine chondrocytes to differentiate into adipocytes in vitro (Heermeier et al., 1994; Hegert et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is based on incomplete conversion efficiency in lineage tracing experiments and citation to literature on skeletal stem cells.

claim: Older studies have demonstrated the ability of murine chondrocytes to differentiate into adipocytes in vitro.
source: Indeed, older studies have demonstrated the ability of murine chondrocytes to differentiate into adipocytes in vitro (Heermeier et al., 1994; Hegert et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous in vitro studies.

claim: Col2a1:CreER cells converted at postnatal day three in mouse were found to give rise to adipocytes in the metaphyseal bone marrow, although a caveat is that Col2a1:CreER marks both chondrocytes and progenitors at early postnatal stages.
source: Further, Col2a1:CreER cells converted at postnatal day three in mouse were found to give rise to adipocytes in the metaphyseal bone marrow, although a caveat is that Col2a1:CreER marks both chondrocytes and progenitors at early postnatal stages (Ono et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous mouse study.

claim: The finding that late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes can re-enter the cell cycle and express lepr suggests that at least some of these cells may dedifferentiate into stem-like cells, which subsequently expand in number and differentiate into osteoblasts and adipocytes.
source: The finding that late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes can re-enter the cell cycle and express lepr suggests that at least some of these cells may dedifferentiate into stem-like cells, which subsequently expand in number and differentiate into osteoblasts and adipocytes.
evidence: This claim is based on BrdU incorporation and lepr expression data shown in Figure 6.

claim: We cannot rule out that some hypertrophic chondrocytes directly change into adipocytes and/or osteoblasts in the absence of cell division (i.e. 'transdifferentiation').
source: We also cannot rule out that some hypertrophic chondrocytes directly change into adipocytes and/or osteoblasts in the absence of cell division (i.e. 'transdifferentiation').
evidence: This claim acknowledges an alternative mechanism that cannot be excluded by the data.

claim: The detection of osteoblasts with strong col2a1a:Histone2A-mCherry signal suggests that in some cases chondrocytes can form osteoblasts with little to no cell division, as otherwise the Histone2A-mCherry signal would have been diluted out with successive cell divisions.
source: Indeed, the detection of osteoblasts with strong col2a1a:Histone2A-mCherry signal suggests that in some cases chondrocytes can form osteoblasts with little to no cell division, as otherwise the Histone2A-mCherry signal would have been diluted out with successive cell divisions.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the Histone2A-mCherry lineage tracing shown in Figure 5 and inference about protein dilution.

claim: Osteoblasts farther from the growth plate tended to have weaker Histone2A-mCherry signal, suggesting proliferation of a progenitor intermediate, and we directly observed late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes undergoing cell division.
source: On the other hand, osteoblasts farther from the growth plate tended to have weaker Histone2A-mCherry signal, suggesting proliferation of a progenitor intermediate, and we directly observed late-stage hypertrophic chondrocytes undergoing cell division.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the Histone2A-mCherry lineage tracing shown in Figure 5 and BrdU incorporation data in Figure 6.

claim: Whereas it has been suggested in mouse that only chondrocytes near the periosteal surface, that is 'borderline chondrocytes', may be capable of lineage plasticity, we detected lineage clones containing growth plate chondrocytes, mesenchymal cells, and adipocytes in the central part of the growth plate, arguing against such a model.
source: Whereas it has been suggested in mouse that only chondrocytes near the periosteal surface, that is 'borderline chondrocytes', may be capable of lineage plasticity (Bianco et al., 1998; Maes et al., 2010), we detected lineage clones containing growth plate chondrocytes, mesenchymal cells, and adipocytes in the central part of the growth plate (Figure 3E,F), arguing against such a model.
evidence: This claim is based on clonal analysis data shown in Figure 3E,F and comparison to a model proposed in mouse studies.

claim: A notable feature of LepR-lineage cells in mice is that they contribute to osteoblasts and adipocytes primarily in postnatal phases, that is when growth plate remodeling is already underway.
source: A notable feature of LepR-lineage cells in mice is that they contribute to osteoblasts and adipocytes primarily in postnatal phases, that is when growth plate remodeling is already underway (Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous mouse study.

claim: We detect endogenous lepr expression in both marrow cells and growth plate chondrocytes in zebrafish.
source: One caveat is that we detect endogenous lepr expression in both marrow cells and growth plate chondrocytes in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The more specific labeling of marrow cells by the LepR-Cre in mouse likely reflects the Cre insertion being in the long LepR isoform (containing exon 18b) that displays more restricted expression than the short isoform.
source: However, the more specific labeling of marrow cells by the LepR-Cre in mouse likely reflects the Cre insertion being in the long LepR isoform (containing exon 18b) that displays more restricted expression than the short isoform (Zhou et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is based on citation to a previous mouse study and knowledge of LepR isoforms.

claim: LepR mRNA and protein has also been reported in chondrocytes of mouse, rat, and human, a finding we confirmed in the postnatal mouse femur, including the same higher expression in immature versus hypertrophic chondrocytes that we observe in zebrafish.
source: Indeed, LepR mRNA and protein has also been reported in chondrocytes of mouse (Hoggard et al., 1997), rat, and human (Morroni et al., 2004), a finding we confirmed in the postnatal mouse femur, including the same higher expression in immature versus hypertrophic chondrocytes that we observe in zebrafish (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and RNAscope data in mouse shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A similar delay in the remodeling of the hypertrophic zone in mouse Mmp9 and zebrafish mmp9 mutants reveals genetic conservation of growth plate remodeling from fish to mammals.
source: A similar delay in the remodeling of the hypertrophic zone in mouse Mmp9 and zebrafish mmp9 mutants reveals genetic conservation of growth plate remodeling from fish to mammals.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of zebrafish mmp9 mutant data in Figure 7 with known mouse Mmp9 mutant phenotypes.

claim: In contrast to mice, we find that Mmp9 in zebrafish appears to function primarily in chondrocytes for growth plate remodeling.
source: In contrast to mice, we find that Mmp9 in zebrafish appears to function primarily in chondrocytes for growth plate remodeling.
evidence: This claim is supported by neural crest transplantation experiments shown in Figure 7E-G.

claim: We also observed rescue of marrow adipocyte number by wild-type chondrocytes, though this had moderate statistical significance (p = 0.06), potentially owing to low sample size (n = 8), the mosaic contribution of wild-type cells to the growth plate, and/or roles of cells outside the growth plate to marrow adipocyte generation.
source: We also observed rescue of marrow adipocyte number by wild-type chondrocytes, though this had moderate statistical significance (p = 0.06), potentially owing to low sample size (n = 8), the mosaic contribution of wild-type cells to the growth plate, and/or roles of cells outside the growth plate to marrow adipocyte generation.
evidence: This claim is based on neural crest transplantation experiments shown in Figure 7E-G and statistical analysis.

claim: In mice, loss of Mmp13 in chondrocytes does result in a growth plate remodeling delay, with global Mmp13 deletion enhancing the remodeling defects of Mmp9 mutants.
source: In mice, loss of Mmp13 in chondrocytes does result in a growth plate remodeling delay, with global Mmp13 deletion enhancing the remodeling defects of Mmp9 mutants (Inada et al., 2004; Stickens et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous mouse studies.

claim: It may be that MMPs are derived from both chondrocytes and invading hematopoietic cells (e.g. osteoclasts), with the relative importance of each cell source varying between zebrafish and mammals.
source: It may be that MMPs are derived from both chondrocytes and invading hematopoietic cells (e.g. osteoclasts), with the relative importance of each cell source varying between zebrafish and mammals.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on comparison of zebrafish and mammalian data.

claim: Compensation by mmp13 might also explain why we detected growth remodeling defects in mmp9 zebrafish mutants at 21 and 27–31 mm SL stages, but not at 17 mm SL.
source: Compensation by mmp13 might also explain why we detected growth remodeling defects in mmp9 zebrafish mutants at 21 and 27–31 mm SL stages, but not at 17 mm SL.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the temporal pattern of mmp9 mutant phenotypes shown in Figure 7.

claim: Mmp9 and Mmp13 have known roles in degrading components of the cartilage extracellular matrix, consistent with our observed loss of collagen-rich matrix in hypertrophic chondrocytes at the edges of the zebrafish growth plate.
source: Mmp9 and Mmp13 have known roles in degrading components of the cartilage extracellular matrix (Page-McCaw et al., 2007), consistent with our observed loss of collagen-rich matrix in hypertrophic chondrocytes at the edges of the zebrafish growth plate.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous studies and histological observations in Figure 1 and Figure 6A.

claim: Secreted Mmp9 may therefore function simply to degrade cartilage matrix and facilitate release of dedifferentiating chondrocytes into the marrow.
source: Secreted Mmp9 may therefore function simply to degrade cartilage matrix and facilitate release of dedifferentiating chondrocytes into the marrow.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on known MMP functions and the observed phenotypes.

claim: Mmp9 has recently been shown to have an additional, non-canonical function in the nucleus for histone H3 tail cleavage.
source: Intriguingly, Mmp9 has recently been shown to have an additional, non-canonical function in the nucleus for histone H3 tail cleavage.
evidence: This claim is based on recent literature about non-canonical MMP functions.

claim: Whereas this has only been demonstrated so far for osteoclasts, it remains possible that Mmp9 could have a similar non-canonical function in altering the chromatin structure of hypertrophic chondrocytes to allow them to acquire new potential.
source: Whereas this has only been demonstrated so far for osteoclasts (Kim et al., 2016), it remains possible that Mmp9 could have a similar non-canonical function in altering the chromatin structure of hypertrophic chondrocytes to allow them to acquire new potential.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on extrapolation from osteoclast studies.

claim: Our data support conservation of mammalian-like growth plate remodeling in zebrafish, which provides new opportunities for better understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which hypertrophic chondrocytes transform into osteoblasts, marrow adipocytes, and potentially adult skeletal stem cells within endochondral bones.
source: In conclusion, our data support conservation of mammalian-like growth plate remodeling in zebrafish, which provides new opportunities for better understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which hypertrophic chondrocytes transform into osteoblasts, marrow adipocytes, and potentially adult skeletal stem cells within endochondral bones.
evidence: This claim is based on the overall findings of the study and their implications for future research.

claim: The two growth plates of Ch are bidirectional with a central zone of compact, proliferative chondrocytes flanked by hypertrophic chondrocytes on either side.
source: Unlike the unidirectional growth plates in the mouse limb, the two growth plates of Ch are bidirectional with a central zone of compact, proliferative chondrocytes flanked by hypertrophic chondrocytes on either side (Paul et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study and anatomical observations.

claim: Unlike in many other fish species, the Ch bone, as with other bones in zebrafish, also contains embedded osteocytes.
source: Unlike in many other fish species, the Ch bone, as with other bones in zebrafish, also contains embedded osteocytes (Witten and Huysseune, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Presumptive resting chondrocytes in the middle of the growth plate express fli1a:GFP.
source: We used fli1a:GFP to label endothelial cells of the vasculature, but we also noticed that presumptive resting chondrocytes in the middle of the growth plate express this transgene.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from confocal imaging shown in Figure 2A.

claim: High-magnification confocal sections at 18 mm SL clearly show fli1a:GFP+ vessels in intimate association with adipocytes and within the Calcein Blue+ bone collar.
source: High-magnification confocal sections at 18 mm SL clearly show fli1a:GFP+ vessels in intimate association with adipocytes and within the Calcein Blue+ bone collar (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The human SOX10 enhancer used for the SOX10:Cre line lacks the second wave of chondrocyte expression seen with the zebrafish regulatory region used for the sox10:CreERT2 line.
source: As a comparison, we used a constitutive Cre driven by a human SOX10 enhancer that drives expression throughout the neural crest lineage (note that this human enhancer lacks the second wave of chondrocyte expression seen with the zebrafish regulatory region used for the sox10:CreERT2 line) (Kague et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study and comparison of expression patterns.

claim: When crossed to the B > R line, the neural crest-specific SOX10:Cre line drives broader conversion in the five dpf head than the later conversion of sox10:CreERT2.
source: When crossed to the B > R line, this neural crest-specific SOX10:Cre line drives broader conversion in the five dpf head than the later conversion of sox10:CreERT2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Analysis of the adult Ch in SOX10:Cre fish shows labeling of all growth plate cartilage, as well as most if not all adipocytes and numerous smaller cells throughout the marrow and cortical bone surface.
source: Analysis of the adult Ch in SOX10:Cre fish shows labeling of all growth plate cartilage, as well as most if not all adipocytes and numerous smaller cells throughout the marrow and cortical bone surface (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: In zebrafish, col2a1a is expressed at high levels in chondrocytes and in weaker levels in osteoblasts and perichondrium.
source: In zebrafish, col2a1a is similarly expressed at high levels in chondrocytes and in weaker levels in osteoblasts and perichondrium, although direct evidence for col2a1a marking osteochondroprogenitors in zebrafish is lacking (Eames et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ocn:GFP, RUNX2:GFP, and sp7:GFP can all be readily distinguished from membrane GFP-CAAX by their much stronger and cytoplasmic expression.
source: Note that ocn:GFP, RUNX2:GFP, and sp7:GFP can all be readily distinguished from membrane GFP-CAAX by their much stronger and cytoplasmic expression.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: The conversion of hypertrophic chondrocytes to osteoblasts and adipocytes could occur in the absence of cell division (i.e. 'transdifferentiation') and/or through partial dedifferentiation into a proliferative progenitor.
source: The conversion of hypertrophic chondrocytes to osteoblasts and adipocytes could occur in the absence of cell division (i.e. 'transdifferentiation') and/or through partial dedifferentiation into a proliferative progenitor.
evidence: This claim presents two possible mechanisms for chondrocyte fate transitions.

claim: The proliferative zone of the growth plate was defined as the central region of compact chondrocytes.
source: The proliferative zone of the growth plate was defined as the central region of compact chondrocytes.
evidence: This claim describes a methodological definition used in the study.
